content.jointProblem: Can a reproducible geospatial pipeline link settlement-level farm policy locations to field-level hail intensity from the 5 km MeteoVoj grid, and use the matched exposure to identify portfolio segments where hail loss is underpriced? The first experiment would test that link against the available geo-tagged claims before any pricing use.

rationale.text: Đorđević's core research is integrating heterogeneous geospatial datasets and harmonising spatial databases, which matches the need to join policy, weather-grid and claims layers.

sources.quote: integrating heterogeneous geospatial datasets from cadastral, topographic, and utility sources
spatial database harmonisation under national and European standards

rationale.text: She works on coordinate reference system transformations and transformation provenance, which is directly relevant to aligning MeteoVoj grids with policy locations and auditing every spatial transformation.

sources.quote: tracks, for each geometry or geometry collection, the source CRS, target CRS, transformation method, parameter set version, and operator identity.

rationale.text: She has operational experience moving a municipal network GIS to PostGIS and her group routinely uses QGIS, PostGIS and FME, matching the company's QGIS/PostgreSQL spatial stack.

sources.quote: supporting the migration of their network GIS from a proprietary format to a PostGIS-based system
The group regularly uses QGIS, PostGIS, FME Workbench, and ArcGIS Pro

rationale.text: She has led a cross-border data-quality and transformation work package, giving her direct experience of quality assurance for multi-source spatial data integration.

sources.quote: Katarina Đorđević led the work package on data quality assessment and transformation infrastructure

risks: A 5 km daily grid may not resolve narrow, fast-moving hail swaths, so apparent field-level exposure may be an artifact of grid resolution.
Settlement-level addresses may make field-level assignment noisy or impossible for a material share of the portfolio, which could weaken any pricing signal.
Transfer gap: the provided record shows flood hazard mapping, not hail intensity mapping; field-level hail inference is the first thing to test.
A prior spatial-risk prototype with a Novi Sad faculty was completed but not integrated into pricing, showing an adoption risk for this work too.
The company's pricing and IT staff are split between operations and new build, so integration ownership and maintenance capacity are not assured.
Limited availability before mid-2026 could delay a joint project or restrict it to a small consulting scope.
questions: Which policy-location fields exist for the 1,200 farm policies (settlement name, address text, parcel identifier, coordinates), and can they be shared under data-protection rules?
What exactly does MeteoVoj supply (hail intensity variable, radar or station basis, daily grid definition), and can historical grids plus independent validation data be provided?
What is the pricing-model interface and what held-out test would count as a credible improvement in identifying underpriced portfolio segments?
Is the expected output a research prototype or a production pipeline, and who on the pricing or IT team owns integration and maintenance?
Can Katarina Đorđević confirm her availability and preferred scope, especially whether a short contract before mid-2026 or a later start is intended?
Are there regulatory, explainability or rating-file constraints on using spatial hail covariates in the pricing model?
